### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.sessions

### Question

1. Open a directory `nvim ~/.config/nvim`
2. Open a few buffers
3. Run `MiniSessions.restart()`
4. Buffers are restored *and* an extra buffer called `nvim` is also created

This buffer matches the directory I opened neovim with in step 1.

I also have this auto command which affects the startup process:

```lua
vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('VimEnter', {
	desc = '  Open file picker when passing a directory: `nvim <dir>`',
	once = true, -- one shot
	nested = true, -- handle other autocmds, like FileType
	callback = function(data)
		local is_dir = vim.fn.isdirectory(data.file) == 1
		if is_dir then
			vim.cmd.cd(data.file)
			MiniPick.builtin.files()
			-- Delete the empty buffer neovim creates when passing a directory.
			vim.api.nvim_buf_delete(data.buf, { force = true })
		end
	end,
})
```

How do I make `MiniSessions.restart()` also delete that empty buffer with directory name?

comment_data.body:
I *think* this is a somewhat unintended behavior of `MiniSessions.restart()`. The reason is that written session always preserves arguments.

The more concise way to reproduce this would be:
- `nvim -- file-a`
- `:bwipeout`
- `:edit file-b`.
- `:lua MiniSessions.restart()`. It now shows both `file-a` and `file-b`.

I'll take a look.

reply_data.body:
Yeah, it seems to be a combination of two things:
- The `:mksession` always preserves argument list. It can be fixed on 'mini.sessions' side.
- The `:restart` command always restarts respecting arguments passed before `--`, like `nvim ~/.config/nvim`. [This is documented](https://neovim.io/doc/user/gui/#_restart-nvim) and *can not* be fixed on 'mini.sessions' side (the responsible [`v:argf` variable](https://neovim.io/doc/user/vvars/#v%3Aargf) is read-only). This behavior [will probably be revised](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/39239#issuecomment-4279290961).

So @andradei, if you want to not have this behavior, my best suggestions are:
- Use `nvim -- ~/.config/nvim` to open directories.
- ~~Append the autocommand from the original comment with `vim.cmd('%argdelete')`. This will clear the argument list on top of deleting the buffer for the opened directory.~~ Not needed anymore since [it is cleared before restarting](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/60b5aaac2f0465d67699702e76b9baebf52cb42f/doc/mini-sessions.txt#L211-L212) (if there is no active session).

    ~~I'll take a closer look if it is a good idea to add this type of "clear arglist" functionality to `MiniSessions.restart()` itself.~~

Yeah, it seems to be a combination of two things:

  • The :mksession always preserves argument list. It can be fixed on 'mini.sessions' side.
  • The :restart command always restarts respecting arguments passed before --, like nvim ~/.config/nvim. This is documented and can not be fixed on 'mini.sessions' side (the responsible v:argf variable is read-only). This behavior will probably be revised.

So @andradei, if you want to not have this behavior, my best suggestions are:

  • Use nvim -- ~/.config/nvim to open directories.

  • Append the autocommand from the original comment with vim.cmd('%argdelete'). This will clear the argument list on top of deleting the buffer for the opened directory. Not needed anymore since it is cleared before restarting (if there is no active session).

    I'll take a closer look if it is a good idea to add this type of "clear arglist" functionality to MiniSessions.restart() itself.

comment_data.body:
@andradei, I noticed that the picker also activates on restart. I could imagine that this is not needed when restarting with mini.sessions.

EDIT: Removed incorrect lua example...
EDIT: Example was correct, but only works with MiniSessions.restart, not with a plain `:restart`...

Using `nvim ~/.config/nvim` still seems to work if the unwanted buffer is deleted inside `UIEnter`:

```lua
require('mini.sessions').setup()
require('mini.pick').setup()

local directory_argument = nil
vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('VimEnter', {
  desc = '  Open file picker when passing a directory: `nvim <dir>`',
  once = true, -- one shot
  nested = true, -- handle other autocmds, like FileType
  callback = function(data)
    local is_dir = vim.fn.isdirectory(data.file) == 1
    if is_dir then
      directory_argument = data.file
      vim.cmd.cd(directory_argument)
      MiniPick.builtin.files()
    end
  end,
})

vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('UIEnter', {
  desc = 'Delete buffer created when passing a directory: `nvim <dir>`',
  once = true,
  callback = function()
    if not directory_argument then return end

    for _, buf in ipairs(vim.api.nvim_list_bufs()) do
      if vim.api.nvim_buf_get_name(buf) == directory_argument then vim.api.nvim_buf_delete(buf, { force = true }) end
    end
  end,
})

```

That's an interesting one. Sounds reasonable, but I'd wait for a more complicated use case that could not be solved without it.

The whole `MiniSessions.restart` is an "emergency measure" until `:restart` can support preserving the layout. And that [is planned](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/38940), only needs an implementation.

reply_data.body: I did try to implement custom `vim.g.minisessions_restart=true`, but realized that it will be available somewhat late: [during after `UIEnter`](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/39282#issuecomment-4639099308) and not during 'init.lua' or `VimEnter` execution. The reason is that `:restart command` executes `command` after attaching all UIs, which is documented in `:h :restart`. So I think it is better to wait for the upstream more proper implementation.
